title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 2nd Truth Divine Speech

questions.question: Which Divine attribute is named at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Divine speech come from?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the verse about the sea becoming ink teach about Allah’s words?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s words have no end.

questions.question: In the passage, what is described as the clearest sign that a being exists?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: Because of that sign, what does this truth strongly testify to about Allah?
questions.answer: It testifies to His existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Which two strong proofs of this truth are named first?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What other kind of proof is given through holy books from heaven?
questions.answer: Sacred revealed books are presented as a wide proof.

questions.question: Which book is described as a very bright and wide-ranging proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage not explain this truth fully here?
questions.answer: Because it sends the reader to other parts of the treatise for fuller explanation.

questions.question: What is enough for the traveler at this point, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The lights and meanings found in the Qur’anic verse about Allah’s words.

questions.question: What does the verse from Surah Al ‘Imran declare about Allah?
questions.answer: That there is no god except Him.

questions.question: Besides Allah, who else is mentioned as bearing witness in that verse?
questions.answer: The angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: What quality is connected with this witness in the verse?
questions.answer: Justice and fairness.

questions.question: Which two Divine qualities are named at the end of that verse?
questions.answer: Mighty and Wise.

questions.question: In the summary of the traveler’s lesson, how is Allah described in relation to existence?
questions.answer: As the Necessary Existent.

questions.question: How is Allah described in relation to oneness in that same summary?
questions.answer: As One and Unique.

questions.question: What belongs to Allah according to that summary besides existence and oneness?
questions.answer: The Most Beautiful Names, the highest attributes, and the loftiest likeness.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in His unity?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent Essence together with all His sacred attributes and beautiful names.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do Allah’s names appear?
questions.answer: They appear through His qualities and actions.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Divine activity such as creating and originating?
questions.answer: It shows the greatness of Divinity through ongoing action.

questions.question: Which two things are linked with creating and bringing into being?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: Which two things are linked with determining, shaping, and regulating?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: Which two things are linked with preserving, managing, and nurturing?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What two qualities describe how these acts are carried out?
questions.answer: Complete order and balance.

questions.question: What is the main difference explained in the Note between the first chapter and the second chapter?
questions.answer: The first chapter treats these truths mainly as proofs of necessary existence, while the second chapter treats them mainly as proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Does the Note say that necessity and unity are separated from each other?
questions.answer: No. Each one also proves the other.

questions.question: What wording change is mentioned to show the difference between the two chapters?
questions.answer: One chapter speaks of testimony, while the other speaks of witnessing.

questions.question: Why does the writer say the second chapter will be brief?
questions.answer: Because different obstacles kept him from giving a long explanation.

questions.question: Where does the writer leave the fuller explanation of these matters?
questions.answer: To other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What topic opens the marked passage?
questions.answer: Divine speech.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute is this topic connected to?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What picture does the Qur’anic verse use to show the greatness of Allah’s words?
questions.answer: It imagines the sea becoming ink.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from that verse about Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: It is limitless.

questions.question: Why is speech so important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because speech is presented as the clearest proof that a speaker exists.

questions.question: What two major truths does Divine speech witness to?
questions.answer: Allah’s existence and His unity.

questions.question: Name one pair of proofs the passage gives for this truth before mentioning books.
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What group of writings is named as another proof?
questions.answer: The sacred books sent from heaven.

questions.question: Which revealed book is given special attention as a shining proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest the reader should do for a fuller discussion?
questions.answer: Look to the other degrees of the treatise.

questions.question: What kind of things are said to be enough for the traveler from the verse?
questions.answer: Its spiritual lights and deep meanings.

questions.question: In the next Qur’anic verse, who bears witness first?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Who joins that witness after Allah?
questions.answer: The angels and those who have knowledge.

questions.question: What central belief do they all witness to?
questions.answer: That only Allah deserves to be taken as god.

questions.question: What moral quality is directly connected to this witness?
questions.answer: Upright justice.

questions.question: What does the passage say this verse alludes to?
questions.answer: The heart of the lesson learned by the traveler.

questions.question: In that lesson, what titles are used to describe Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: One and Unique.

questions.question: What does the lesson say belongs to Allah in terms of names and attributes?
questions.answer: The Beautiful Names and the supreme attributes.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what agrees together in pointing to Allah’s necessary existence?
questions.answer: All His sacred attributes and all His beautiful names.

questions.question: Through what are Allah’s names said to become manifest?
questions.answer: Through His active qualities and deeds.

questions.question: What does constant Divine activity show according to the lesson?
questions.answer: The greatness of Divinity appearing through lordship.

questions.question: What three kinds of action are linked with will and power?
questions.answer: Bringing into being, creating, and making.

questions.question: What kinds of action are linked with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, regulating, and turning things in order.

questions.question: What kinds of action are linked with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Managing, preserving, arranging, directing, and providing.

questions.question: What two features of the universe’s order are mentioned at the end of that list?
questions.answer: Harmony and balance.

questions.question: In the Note, how are the truths of the first chapter mainly classified?
questions.answer: As proofs of Necessary Existence.

questions.question: In the Note, how are the truths of the second chapter mainly classified?
questions.answer: As proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: What relationship between unity and necessity is stated clearly in the Note?
questions.answer: Each one proves the other.

questions.question: Why was the explanation of the second chapter not expanded in the same way?
questions.answer: Obstacles forced the writer to keep it short.

questions.question: Which attribute of Allah is the focus of this passage?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: What comes from this attribute according to the opening line?
questions.answer: Divine discourse.

questions.question: What idea about Allah’s words is taken from the verse about the sea and ink?
questions.answer: His words are beyond limit.

questions.question: What human sign is used as an example to show that a being exists?
questions.answer: Speaking.

questions.question: If speech shows a speaker, what does Divine speech show in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: Why is this testimony described as infinite?
questions.answer: Because the Divine speech being discussed is infinite.

questions.question: What two forms of Divine communication are named as strong evidence?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What larger body of evidence is added after those two?
questions.answer: The holy books sent by Allah.

questions.question: Which final proof in this list is described as especially brilliant and complete?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the effect of sending the reader to other degrees?
questions.answer: It shows that fuller proof has already been discussed elsewhere.

questions.question: What truth does that verse support along with the earlier testimonies?
questions.answer: The truth of Allah’s existence and oneness shown through His speech.

questions.question: In the verse from Surah Al ‘Imran, what is Allah doing?
questions.answer: Bearing witness to His own oneness.

questions.question: Which two groups support this witness?
questions.answer: Angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: Which two Divine names end the verse?
questions.answer: The Mighty and the Wise.

questions.question: In the statement from the Nineteenth Degree, what title shows that Allah cannot fail to exist?
questions.answer: Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What title shows that Allah has no partner and no equal?
questions.answer: One and Unique.

questions.question: What three things are especially said to belong to Allah in that statement?
questions.answer: Beautiful Names, supreme attributes, and the highest similitude.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in unity according to that statement?
questions.answer: His Essence, together with the agreement of His attributes and names.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the names being manifested through qualities and deeds?
questions.answer: Allah’s names become known through what He does and how He acts.

questions.question: Which actions are connected with will and power?
questions.answer: Creating, originating, making, and bringing things into existence.

questions.question: Which actions are connected with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, directing, and arranging change.

questions.question: Which actions are connected with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Spending out provision, protecting, organizing, managing, and nurturing.

questions.question: What do complete order and balance add to the argument?
questions.answer: They strengthen the proof that these actions come from perfect Divine rule.

questions.question: According to the Note, why were these truths treated first as proofs of existence?
questions.answer: Because they show existence more openly and directly.

questions.question: Why will they be treated in the second chapter as proofs of unity?
questions.answer: Because there they show oneness more directly, even though they also imply necessity.

questions.question: What writing choice marks this shift in emphasis?
questions.answer: A repeated phrase about testimony is changed to a repeated phrase about witnessing.

questions.question: What reason is given for the brief style at the end of the Note?
questions.answer: The writer says obstacles prevented a full explanation.

questions.question: What is the source of Divine discourse in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s attribute of Speech.

questions.question: How does the verse about the sea help the reader understand Divine speech?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s words cannot be exhausted.

questions.question: What everyday sign is used to show that someone exists?
questions.answer: The fact that he speaks.

questions.question: How does the passage move from that sign to a belief about Allah?
questions.answer: It says Divine speech is a never-ending proof that Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: What are the first two evidences listed for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What written sources are also named as evidence?
questions.answer: Sacred books from heaven.

questions.question: Which book is singled out as the most radiant and wide proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why are readers directed elsewhere for more detail?
questions.answer: Because those other sections explain and establish this truth more fully.

questions.question: What is enough for the traveler and the readers at this point?
questions.answer: A brief share of the verse’s light and meaning.

questions.question: What statement about Allah is repeated in the verse from Surah Al ‘Imran?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Him.

questions.question: Who are the two created groups that also testify to this truth?
questions.answer: The angels and those who possess knowledge.

questions.question: What does the phrase about standing in justice show about Allah’s witness?
questions.answer: It shows that His witness is tied to perfect justice.

questions.question: Which two qualities of Allah close the verse?
questions.answer: Might and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say this verse points toward?
questions.answer: The main lesson the traveler learned at that sacred stopping place.

questions.question: In that lesson, what does calling Allah the Necessary Existent teach?
questions.answer: That His existence is certain and not dependent on anything else.

questions.question: What does calling Allah One and Unique teach?
questions.answer: That He has no partner and no second.

questions.question: What special honors of Allah are mentioned right after that?
questions.answer: His Beautiful Names, His highest attributes, and His most exalted likeness.

questions.question: What gives agreement in pointing to Allah’s necessary existence?
questions.answer: All His sacred all-encompassing attributes and all His beautiful names.

questions.question: Through what are those names said to be displayed?
questions.answer: Through His ruling qualities and active deeds.

questions.question: What larger reality is shown through these deeds?
questions.answer: The greatness of Divinity appearing within lordship.

questions.question: Which pair goes with bringing things into existence and creating?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: Which pair goes with shaping and regulating?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: Which pair goes with preserving and nurturing?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What two words describe the way these Divine acts appear in the world?
questions.answer: Order and balance.

questions.question: In the Note, what do the truths in the first chapter indicate in addition to existence?
questions.answer: They also show Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: Why were they still counted there mainly as proofs of Necessary Existence?
questions.answer: Because that aspect was more obvious and direct.

questions.question: In the second chapter, what will be the main emphasis instead?
questions.answer: Divine unity.

questions.question: What important connection between the two teachings does the Note make clear?
questions.answer: Unity proves necessity, and necessity proves unity.

questions.question: What personal limitation does the writer mention at the end?
questions.answer: He wanted to explain more, but had to be brief because of obstacles.

questions.question: What truth is introduced first in this marked section?
questions.answer: The truth of Divine speech.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute is directly tied to that truth?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: What does the Qur’anic image of an ocean of ink suggest?
questions.answer: That Allah’s words are endless.

questions.question: What sign is said to most clearly show that a being is really there?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: What does that make Divine speech into?
questions.answer: A vast proof of Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: Which two forms of guidance from Allah are named as strong supports for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What collection of evidence is added after those two supports?
questions.answer: The holy and heavenly books.

questions.question: What special place does the Qur’an have among those proofs?
questions.answer: It is described as the brightest and most complete proof.

questions.question: Why does the passage avoid a long explanation here?
questions.answer: Because the detailed proof is already discussed in other sections.

questions.question: What is said to be enough for the traveler who stops here?
questions.answer: The insight and spiritual meaning in the verse itself.

questions.question: In the next verse, who testifies first to the truth of tawhid?
questions.answer: Allah Himself.

questions.question: Who are named after Allah as witnesses?
questions.answer: The angels and the people of knowledge.

questions.question: What does their shared witness center on?
questions.answer: Allah’s exclusive right to be worshipped.

questions.question: What trait of Allah’s rule is highlighted in that same verse?
questions.answer: Justice.

questions.question: What two Divine names at the end give a sense of strength and wisdom together?
questions.answer: The Mighty and the Wise.

questions.question: The passage says this verse hints at the core of what lesson?
questions.answer: The lesson the traveler learned at that sacred station.

questions.question: In that lesson, what words show Allah’s absolute singleness?
questions.answer: One and Unique.

questions.question: What words show that Allah’s existence is not borrowed or dependent?
questions.answer: Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What three honors are said to belong to Allah?
questions.answer: The Beautiful Names, the Supreme Attributes, and the Most Sublime Similitude.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what gives united testimony to Allah’s necessary existence?
questions.answer: His sacred attributes and beautiful names, together with their manifestations.

questions.question: Where are these manifestations seen?
questions.answer: In His qualities and His deeds.

questions.question: What broad truth is said to appear in the ongoing acts of creating and originating?
questions.answer: The greatness of Divinity within the manifestation of lordship.

questions.question: What supports acts like creating and bringing into being?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: What supports acts like determining and regulating?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: What supports acts like preserving and nurturing?
questions.answer: Intention or purpose, and mercy.

questions.question: What do perfect arrangement and measured balance show?
questions.answer: That these acts come from a flawless Divine order.

questions.question: In the Note, what is said about the truths in the nineteen degrees of the first chapter?
questions.answer: They prove Necessary Existence and also, through their wide scope, Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What new label is given to these truths in the second chapter?
questions.answer: Proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: How does the Note explain the relationship between those two kinds of proof?
questions.answer: Each one contains and supports the other.

questions.question: What practical reason is given for the short explanation in the second chapter?
questions.answer: The writer faced obstacles and had to summarize.

questions.question: What subject does the passage begin by naming before anything else?
questions.answer: Divine discourse.

questions.question: From which attribute does this discourse proceed?
questions.answer: From the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the quoted Qur’anic verse imply about the number of Allah’s words?
questions.answer: They cannot be counted to an end.

questions.question: In the passage’s reasoning, what is the strongest outward sign that someone exists?
questions.answer: His speaking.

questions.question: What are the first two named evidences for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What kind of books are also mentioned as a wide proof?
questions.answer: Holy books from heaven.

questions.question: Which one book is presented as the most brilliant and fullest proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage do instead of repeating all those proofs in detail?
questions.answer: It refers the reader to other degrees where they are already explained.

questions.question: What is enough at this point for the traveler in the passage?
questions.answer: The meanings and lights found in the lofty verse.

questions.question: What key belief is clearly stated in the verse from Surah Al ‘Imran?
questions.answer: That no god exists except Allah.

questions.question: Which beings join in this witness besides Allah?
questions.answer: Angels and possessors of knowledge.

questions.question: What does their presence suggest about knowledge and faith?
questions.answer: True knowledge supports belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What phrase in that verse points to Allah’s fairness in rule?
questions.answer: The phrase about upholding justice.

questions.question: Which two Divine names are given at the end of the verse?
questions.answer: The Mighty and the Wise.

questions.question: What is this verse said to allude to in relation to the traveler?
questions.answer: The heart of the lesson he learned at that station.

questions.question: In the declaration that follows, what title shows that Allah must exist?
questions.answer: Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What titles show that Allah is absolutely one?
questions.answer: One and Unique.

questions.question: What possessions of Allah are listed right after those titles?
questions.answer: His Beautiful Names, His Supreme Attributes, and His Most Sublime Similitude.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in His unity according to this declaration?
questions.answer: The necessarily existent Essence with the agreement of all His sacred attributes and beautiful names.

questions.question: Through what are His names shown forth?
questions.answer: Through His controlling qualities and actions.

questions.question: What kinds of acts are tied to will and power?
questions.answer: Bringing into existence, creating, producing, and originating.

questions.question: What kinds of acts are tied to choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, directing, and ordering change.

questions.question: What kinds of acts are tied to purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Distributing, preserving, organizing, managing, and sustaining.

questions.question: What two words describe the excellence of these acts in the world?
questions.answer: Order and equilibrium.

questions.question: According to the Note, what did the truths in the first chapter prove most openly?
questions.answer: Necessary Existence.

questions.question: What will the same truths prove more openly in the second chapter?
questions.answer: Divine unity.

questions.question: Does the Note treat unity and necessity as unrelated topics or linked truths?
questions.answer: Linked truths.

questions.question: What final explanation is given for why the writer stays concise?
questions.answer: He intended more detail, but obstacles forced him to be brief and leave fuller explanation to other parts.
